title: Job 30: They That Are Younger Than I Have Me In Derision
body:
Read the chapter → [Job 30](/bible/job/30)

**[Job 30:1-3](/bible/job/30#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/job/30#v1)</sup> But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/job/30#v2)</sup> Yea, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/job/30#v3)</sup> For want and famine they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.

- Now they that are younger than Job have him in derision, whose fathers he would have disdained to set with the dogs of his flock. This goes into Esau. Their fathers were not even good enough to sit with Job's animals.
- Their strength of hands profited Job nothing, and in them old age was perished. For want and famine they were solitary, fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.
  - **[Genesis 25:30](/bible/genesis/25#v30)**
    > <sup>[30](/bible/genesis/25#v30)</sup> And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.

    Esau is the one who sold his birthright for pottage, the father of the base people Job describes.
- There is a class, believed to be by Deacon Ikkos or the Bishop, that went into the history of how Esau was chased into the mountains and was eating the lights out of the drawers while the drawers disintegrated on them. These were the masked people.

**[Job 30:4-8](/bible/job/30#v4)**
> <sup>[4](/bible/job/30#v4)</sup> Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/job/30#v5)</sup> They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/job/30#v6)</sup> To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/job/30#v7)</sup> Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/job/30#v8)</sup> They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.

- Who cut up mallows by the bushes and juniper roots for their meat. They were driven forth from among men, they cried after them as after a thief, to dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth and in the rocks.
- That is why the dye said it dwelleth in the clifts of the rocks. Among the bushes they brayed, under the nettles they were gathered together. They were children of fools, children of base men, viler than the earth.
- Everything Esau was, they were the original caveman, the cave dwellers living in the clefts of the rocks, eating lights off themselves and wearing their drawers till they disintegrated, while we were actually ruling at that time.

**[Job 30:9-15](/bible/job/30#v9)**
> <sup>[9](/bible/job/30#v9)</sup> And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/job/30#v10)</sup> They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/job/30#v11)</sup> Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/job/30#v12)</sup> Upon my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/job/30#v13)</sup> They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/job/30#v14)</sup> They came upon me as a wide breaking in of waters: in the desolation they rolled themselves upon me.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/job/30#v15)</sup> Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud.

- Now Job is their song and their byword. Those same base people who used to be subject to us, whom we had under us, now we are the ones subject to them. They call us African-American, Negro, the Gentiles, heathens, when they are really the actual evil.
- They abhor Job, flee far from him, and spare not to spit in his face, because God has loosed his cord and afflicted him. Upon his right hand rise the youth, they push away his feet and raise up against him the ways of their destruction.
- They mar his path, they set forward his calamity, they have no helper. They came upon him as a wide breaking in of waters and in the desolation rolled themselves upon him. Terrors are turned upon him.

**[Job 30:16-19](/bible/job/30#v16)**
> <sup>[16](/bible/job/30#v16)</sup> And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/job/30#v17)</sup> My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/job/30#v18)</sup> By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/job/30#v19)</sup> He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.

- Now Job's soul is poured out upon him and the days of affliction have taken hold upon him. His bones are pierced in him in the night season and his sinews take no rest.
- By the great force of his disease is his garment changed; it binds him about as the collar of his coat. He has been cast into the mire and has become like dust and ashes.

**[Job 30:20-24](/bible/job/30#v20)**
> <sup>[20](/bible/job/30#v20)</sup> I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/job/30#v21)</sup> Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/job/30#v22)</sup> Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride upon it, and dissolvest my substance.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/job/30#v23)</sup> For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/job/30#v24)</sup> Howbeit he will not stretch out his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.

- Job cries unto the Most High and is not heard; he stands up and is not regarded. God is become cruel to him, and with His strong hand opposes Himself against him.
- God lifts him up to the wind, causes him to ride upon it, and dissolves his substance. Job knows God will bring him to death and to the house appointed for all living. Yet He will not stretch out His hand to the grave, though they cry in His destruction.

**[Job 30:25-31](/bible/job/30#v25)**
> <sup>[25](/bible/job/30#v25)</sup> Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/job/30#v26)</sup> When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/job/30#v27)</sup> My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/job/30#v28)</sup> I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/job/30#v29)</sup> I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/job/30#v30)</sup> My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/job/30#v31)</sup> My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

- Did not Job weep for him that was in trouble, and was not his soul grieved for the poor? When he looked for good, evil came; when he waited for light, there came darkness. His bowels boiled and rested not; the days of affliction prevented him.
- He went mourning without the sun, he stood up and cried in the congregation. He is a brother to dragons and a companion to owls. His skin is black upon him and his bones are burned with heat. His harp is turned to mourning and his organ into the voice of them that weep.
